chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hazhaz, on the authority of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: 'I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:'

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, has provided the sustenance of the believers from where they do not expect, and this is that when the servant does not know the source of his sustenance, his supplication increases.
ai.seo_question: Why does a believer's supplication increase when they do not know the source of their sustenance?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this as a divine wisdom where the uncertainty of provision's origin fosters continuous supplication (dua), preventing believers from becoming complacent or attributing sustenance solely to worldly means. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining spiritual humility and constant awareness of God's hidden blessings (ni'mah) in daily life.
